key_idea: Each node's weight appears in only two constraints (its own star and its parent's), so the constraints form a tree b-matching that a deepest-first greedy solves: give each free node min(residual of its star, residual of its parent's star).
sketch: Set cap[v]=K for each star (v plus its children), subtract fixed weights from the node's own star and its parent's; any negative capacity means -1. Process free nodes in reverse BFS order: when v is processed all its children are done, so v is the only remaining variable in star v, and an exchange argument shows assigning min(res[v], res[parent]) is optimal (any weight on a sibling or the parent could be shifted to v without loss). The root only has its own star. O(N), 64-bit total (up to 2e14). Verified against exhaustive search on small trees.
